robot: Unitree H1 humanoid with two Shadow dexterous hands (HumanoidBench, MuJoCo): 61 position servos, no walking controller

frame.suite: the robot's pelvis frame (the service gives no root pose)
frame.base_text: the pelvis frame: +X the way the pelvis faces, +Y left, +Z up (no part here takes an end-effector pose, and the service reports no position of the robot in the room)

legs.note: left_hip_yaw, left_hip_roll, left_hip_pitch, left_knee, left_ankle, then the same five on the right; normalized servo targets (-1..1)

torso.note: the torso yaw servo; normalized servo target (-1..1)

left.note: left_shoulder_pitch, left_shoulder_roll, left_shoulder_yaw, left_elbow, left_wrist_yaw; normalized servo targets (-1..1)

right.note: right_shoulder_pitch, right_shoulder_roll, right_shoulder_yaw, right_elbow, right_wrist_yaw; normalized servo targets (-1..1)

left_hand.note: the left Shadow hand's 20 servos (lh_A_*): wrist WRJ2, WRJ1, then the fingers; each *J0 servo drives a tendon that bends a finger's two distal joints together; normalized servo targets (-1..1)

right_hand.note: the right Shadow hand's 20 servos (rh_A_*), same order as the left hand; normalized servo targets (-1..1)

resets.note: Each episode has its own control-step budget; only the last episode is graded, and a success ends the run at once.

notes: Every joint command here is HumanoidBench's own normalized servo target, not an angle: -1 and +1 command the two ends of that actuator's range (range_rad of action type joint_position in describe_robot's spec_file), linearly, so 0 is mid-range, not 0 rad; values outside -1..1 are clipped. The state reports measured joint angles in radians (proprio_now, layout proprio_layout: every joint's angle, then its velocity, then the pelvis IMU), so the two scales differ; the hands' *J0 tendon servos command the sum of two joint angles. At the start of each episode every servo targets 0 rad, which is (-(lo + hi) / (hi - lo)) on the normalized scale. move_robot and execute_trajectory space joint keep the parts you do not name at the last command you sent: until you have sent one in an episode (also after a reset), send a whole 61-number row with execute_trajectory space native (action_type joint_position). There is no walking or balance controller: standing, stepping and keeping balance all come from the servo targets you send, 50 per second of robot time (control period 0.02 s). Time passes only inside calls; the episode ends on success, a fall, a dropped object where the task has one, or its last control step, and the service only says that it ended and why.
